summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for elective bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and mainstem bronchi, along with tracheostomy tube replacement, due to recurrent tracheobronchial stenosis from Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. The procedure was completed without complications, though the planned custom tracheostomy tube could not be placed due to compression and was replaced with a standard Portex 9 tube. Post-procedure, he experienced mild pain at the trach site, managed with acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and short-term oxycodone. He remained stable throughout the admission, with improving lung volumes on imaging and normalization of white blood cell count. He maintained oxygenation without distress and was discharged home on day three with instructions to continue all home medications, including inhaled tobramycin and fluticasone, and to follow up with rheumatology and infectious disease. Plans were made for future evaluation regarding possible stent placement in the left mainstem bronchus.
